newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: Bula and Canadian firm await Libyan accord.
newsitem.headline: Bula and Canadian firm await Libyan accord.

text.p: Irish-based exploration company Bula resources said negotiations with an unnamed major Canadian oil firm on a hydrocarbon exploration agreement with Libya were being considered for final regulatory approval.
Bula said in a statement it had negotiated a farm-out agreement with the Canadian firm to join Bula in exploring for hydrocarbons in blocks G and U in the Sirte and Ghadames basins.

When its Exploration and Sharing Agreement (EPSA) with the National Oil Corporation of Libya (NOC) is ratified, the Canadian company will carry Bula's costs for the entire exploration phase and provide finance for the development programme "for this area of massive potential", it said.
The statement did not name the Canadian company involved.
Bula said the EPSA for blocks G and U had led to extensive negotiations between Bula, the Libyan authorities and the Canadian company.
"This has resulted in the EPSA reaching the state where it is being considered for final regulatory approval, Bula said.
The company said it had also reached agreement "with a major integrated central European oil company" to apply for additional prime acreage in Libya.
Negotiations with the NOC for an EPSA are expected to conclude shortly, it said.
The principal area included is the CC block in the Sirte basin which contains the Chadar Oil, Gas and Condesnsate fields, it said.
